thread:
Alex Chen: heads-up — support escalated two customers in the last 24h about sudden 429s + long tails during short bursts. creating a thread to capture test plan and decide sane default RPM/TPM + burst windows.

Priya Nair: details? are these auth errors or true rate-limit rejections?

Alex Chen: both. one was quota exhaustion (customer hit a big batch job, burned tokens), other looked like transient quota enforcement when a customer burst-hit multiple endpoints. support ticket refs: #4321 (billing), #4330 (latency).

Samir Patel: saw a reproducer from #4330 — they ran parallel client forks hitting /v1/chat and /v1/embed at same time. burst ~6k rps for ~20s, then drop. our shard started returning 429 + 503 combos.

Maria Lopez: 6k rps sounds huge for a single org key — was this on dedicated or hosted?

Samir Patel: hosted, us-east. single API key across 12 hosts (they forked process per core). headers showed no token misuse, legit traffic.

Alex Chen: support reported latency spikes before 429s; traces show queue buildup then token limiter kicking in. likely our token-bucket + burst window misaligned with request batching and backend queue thresholds.

Priya Nair: can we get an internal load test that mimics that pattern? short severe bursts, multi-endpoint fanout, and token-heavy calls (long responses)

Samir Patel: I ran an internal smoke yesterday. config below. results attached.

Samir Patel: ```bash
# quick repro (vegeta)
echo "POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat" > targets.txt
cat targets.txt | vegeta attack -rate=500 -duration=30s | vegeta report
# NOTE: for real tests we spin many clients concurrently and vary QPS and token sizes
```

Samir Patel: initial run (single endpoint) — sustained 500 rps for 30s: 200 OK 100%, p95 latency 140ms.

Samir Patel: burst run — pre-warm then spike to 6k rps for 20s: p95 1.2s, 429s 8%, 503s 2% (backend saturation), token usage spiked ~3x normal.

Priya Nair: interesting. do we have TPM numbers for those runs? long responses mean more tokens and slower KV cache hits.

Samir Patel: TPM ~120k during spike (approx). regular sustained runs ~40k TPM.

Alex Chen: ok this suggests we need both request-rate limits and token-rate limits with burst allowances. current config: RPM 3k per org, TPM 50k per org, burst window 60s with burst multiplier 4. seems those defaults are too aggressive for some shared-hosting clusters.

Maria Lopez: what's our cheap/easy fallback today? we have per-route fallbacks to smaller model + region fallback. but 429s still user-visible.

Priya Nair: action item: design a load matrix and run canonical tests to pick new defaults. matrix should include combinations: sustained low (200-1k rps), medium (1k-3k), spike-short (5k-10k for 10-30s), multi-endpoint concurrent, high TPM payloads (avg response 1k tokens).

Alex Chen: propose test plan (short):
1) baseline: 10m @ 500rps single endpoint (chat)
2) multi-route: 5m @ 500rps each to /chat + /embed (simulate fanout)
3) spike: 20s spikes to 5k, 8k, 10k from 100 client IPs
4) token-heavy: 1k-token avg responses, spikes similar to (3)
5) repeated bursts: 6x spikes per hour to test refill behavior and burst-window enforcement

Samir Patel: will run this in staging (cluster-config matches prod CPU/RAM but reduced GPU). any tooling suggestions? I wrote a small harness that orchestrates vegeta + our request-replayer. can push to eng-infra repo.

Maria Lopez: include a test that varies burst window (30s, 60s, 120s) and multiplier (x2, x4, x8) to see which combos avoid cascading 503s.

Priya Nair: also test per-key vs per-org quotas: some customers share keys across many processes; per-key limit might be too restrictive while per-org might be more fair.

Support Bot: note: ticket #4321 updated — customer provided timeline & request IDs. attaching to thread.

Alex Chen: during tests let's capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, 429 rate, 503 rate, backend queue length, token burn rate, and our limiter refill state (we can log bucket tokens).

Samir Patel: capturing limiter internal metrics — added logs: LIMITER:{org}:{bucket} token_count, last_refill_ts in traces. will aggregate.

Priya Nair: hypothesis: current burst window 60s + multiplier 4 allows 12k RPM equivalent for short period, but our backend queuing can't absorb sustained microbursts from many connections leading to timeouts and 503s. we should pick defaults that keep user-visible errors under 0.5% for canonical workloads.

Maria Lopez: agreed. target for hosted-tier defaults: <=0.5% 429/503 during canonical burst (10-30s), p95 < 500ms for non-burst. for enterprise/dedicated tiers we can loosen.

Samir Patel: first quick run queued. I'll post results in thread. rough ETA 2h for full matrix run in staging (parallel runs).

Alex Chen: decision framework we should follow after results:
- if 429s >0.5% for canonical burst -> reduce burst multiplier or shrink burst window
- if 503s >0.5% during bursts -> backend autoscale policy or routing fallback needs work; prefer routing fallback to cheaper variant before rejecting
- if TPM correlates strongly with errors -> tighten TPM defaults or improve KV cache to reduce token regen

Priya Nair: also add one run that simulates billing-break: repeated high-token calls that exhaust monthly token quota quickly to ensure billing protections trigger and customers get clear error messages (401/402-style) not confusing 429s.

Support Bot: ticket #4330: customer asks for recommended per-key rate-limiting best-practices. assigned to Alex.

Alex Chen: noted. will draft a one-pager with recommended client patterns: exponential backoff, jitter, token batching, and using per-route quotas.

Samir Patel: results (first wave) — spike to 8k for 20s: 429 6.9%, 503 1.7%, p95 1.35s. burst-window=60s, multiplier=4. changing multiplier to 2 (keeping window) reduced 429s to 3.2% but p95 still 900ms.

Maria Lopez: interesting — multiplier=2 lowers 429s but still high. try reduce window to 30s + multiplier=3 maybe? that reduces sustained effective capacity but shortens refill.

Samir Patel: running 30s window + x3 now.

Samir Patel: 30s+x3 results: 429 1.1%, 503 0.9%, p95 720ms. repeated bursts (6x/hr) -> 429 accumulates to 1.8% across hour.

Priya Nair: that's closer. baseline tradeoff: user experience vs allowing short big bursts. For hosted default we can pick 30s+x3 and RPM=1500, TPM=60k. enterprise customers get higher by contract.

Alex Chen: proposal: hosted default -> RPM 1500/org, TPM 60k/org, burst window 30s, burst multiplier 3. implement in config and run a canary rollout to 5% of traffic next week.

Maria Lopez: add observability flag: measure 429/503 and latency per-customer during canary and automatic rollback if 429/503 >0.7% or p95 >800ms for 5m.

Samir Patel: will create canary deploy PR and include the test harness so we can replay incidents.

Support Bot: added note to tickets #4321 and #4330 that we're testing and plan canary.

Alex Chen: outstanding action items:
- Samir: run full matrix, push test artifacts + raw metrics (ETA EOD)
- Priya: draft one-pager on client best-practices + recommended SDK backoff defaults (ETA tomorrow)
- Maria: draft canary rollback thresholds and chart in console (ETA 2 days)
- Alex: create config PR to change hosted defaults behind feature flag (ETA 3 days)

Samir Patel: copying results and logs here: https://internal.redwood/run/rt-1821 (will attach CSV + traces).

Priya Nair: thanks everyone. once canary is good we'll update support KB and billing protection messaging.

Alex Chen: closing loop — we should also add an automated load-test that runs once per week with synthetic bursts and alerts if error-rate increases vs baseline. will add to eng-sre playbook.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued for feature/limiter-canary -> staging (ID: deploy-1987) :rocket:

Maria Lopez: nice. I'll start drafting the SLO thresholds doc.

Samir Patel: will post final matrix CSV and a short summary when done.

Alex Chen: thanks all — good thread. feel free to ping me if you spot anything odd in the staging runs. :thumbsup:
